title: User Journey & Persona Analysis
insights:
USER JOURNEY ANALYSIS OF BUS TICKET BOOKING APP

The dataset comprises a total of 44,031 events from 499 users over a period from December 24, 2025, to January 20, 2026. The analysis focuses on user interactions within the app, particularly around key milestones in the ticket booking process.

USER TYPE BREAKDOWN

The breakdown of user types is as follows:

  • Browsers: 178 users (35.7%)
  • Shoppers: 170 users (34.1%)
  • Attempters: 27 users (5.4%)
  • Bookers: 9 users (1.8%)

This funnel shape indicates a significant drop-off at each stage of the user journey, suggesting that while many users show initial intent to search for tickets, a much smaller percentage proceed to complete a booking. The conversion rate from search to booking is notably low at 1.8%, highlighting potential barriers in the selection and payment processes.

FRICTION IMPACT

Out of the users analyzed:

  • Users who faced payment failures: 17 (3.4%)
  • Users who faced app errors: 0 (0%)

The presence of payment failures indicates a significant churn driver, as 3.4% of users encountered issues that likely deterred them from completing their bookings. This suggests that improving the payment process could enhance overall conversion rates.

POWER USERS VS CASUALS

Based on the stats, a "high-intent" user can be defined as one who progresses beyond the initial search stage and engages with the seat selection and payment initiation. Specifically, users who select a seat (Shoppers) or attempt payment (Attempters) exhibit higher intent compared to Browsers. The distinction is clear: Browsers show interest but do not commit, while Shoppers and Attempters demonstrate a willingness to engage further in the booking process.

PERSONALIZATION SUGGESTIONS FOR BROWSERS

To convert Browsers into Shoppers, the following strategies could be implemented:

  • Enhanced Seat Selection Experience: Introduce a feature that allows Browsers to view seat availability and pricing more dynamically, perhaps with visual aids or recommendations based on their previous searches.
  • Incentives for Engagement: Offer limited-time discounts or promotional codes to Browsers who return to the app after their initial search, encouraging them to select a seat and proceed to payment.
